headline: Iran claims missile strike on US military barracks in Jordan
summary: The IRGC claims multiple US soldiers were killed and attack helicopters destroyed in a retaliatory strike on Camp Tattin, following US air strikes in southern Iran.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have launched a ballistic missile attack on the US Marine barracks at 'Camp Tattin' in Jordan on Tuesday night.
The IRGC stated in a statement published by IRIB, Iran's state broadcaster, that the attack resulted in many US soldiers being killed and several installations and attack helicopters being destroyed.
The strike in Jordan was a response to US air strikes that targeted several areas in southern Iran on Tuesday.

According to Al Jazeera, citing Fars News Agency, US forces targeted a residential area in the coastal city of Kuhestak in Hormozgan province, as well as other locations including Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Chabahar, Jask, Sirik, Lavan, and Asaluyeh.
This marks the first direct exchange of attacks between the two nations since July, following threats from US President Donald Trump to hit Tehran own 'hard'.
President Trump has warned that if Iran continues to retaliate, the US will respond with even more severe strikes.
caption:
Iran claims multiple US soldiers killed in missile strike on Jordan barracks. This follows a series of US air strikes across southern Iran.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have launched a ballistic missile attack on the US Marine barracks at 'Camp Tattin' in Jordan on Tuesday night.

The IRGC stated in a statement published by IRIB, Iran's state broadcaster, that the attack resulted in many US soldiers being killed and several installations and attack helicopters being destroyed.

The strike in Jordan was a response to US air strikes that targeted several areas in southern Iran on Tuesday.

According to Al Jazeera, citing Fars News Agency, US forces targeted a residential area in the coastal city of Kuhestak in Hormozgan province, as well as other locations including Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Chabahar, Jask, Sirik, Lavan, and Asaluyeh.

This marks the first direct exchange of attacks between the two nations since July, following threats from US President Donald Trump to hit Tehran own 'hard'.

President Trump has warned that if Iran continues to retaliate, the US will respond with even more severe strikes.

headline_marked: Tawhid Hridoy [[hits double century abroad]] against South Africa 'A'
headline: Tawhid Hridoy hits double century abroad against South Africa 'A'
summary: The Bangladesh 'A' skipper joins Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, and Shahriar Hossain in an elite list of batters to score first-class double tons overseas.
details: Bangladesh 'A' captain Tawhid Hridoy scored a brilliant double century against South Africa 'A' on the third day of the second four-day match at NWC Oval in Potchefstroom.
Hridoy reached his double hundred off 335 balls, hitting 22 fours and a six, helping the visitors close in on the hosts' first-innings total.
This marks Hridoy's second double century in first-class cricket, having previously scored 217 for BCB South Zone against North Zone in Chattogram.
The 24-year-old batter now joins an elite group of Bangladesh batters to score first-class double centuries abroad, including Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, and Shahriar Hossain.
In addition to Hridoy's feat, Jaker Ali narrowly missed a century with 94 off 168 balls, while Mohammad Saifuddin contributed 87 off 171 balls.
Bangladesh 'A' finished the day's play on 471 for six, still trailing South Africa Africa 'A' by 41 runs after the hosts posted 512 in their first innings.
caption:
Tawhid Hridoy joins the elite list! 🏏

Bangladesh 'A' captain Tawhid Hridoy scored a brilliant double century against South Africa 'A' on the third day of the second four-day match at NWC Oval in Potchefstroom.

Hridoy reached his double hundred off 335 balls, hitting 22 fours and a six, helping the visitors close in on the hosts' first-innings total.

This marks Hridoy's second double century in first-class cricket, having previously scored 217 for BCB South Zone against North Zone in Chattogram.

The 24-year-old batter now joins an elite group of Bangladesh batters to score first-class double centuries abroad, including Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, and Shahriar Hossain.

In addition to Hridoy's feat, Jaker Ali narrowly missed a century with 94 off 168 balls, while Mohammad Saifuddin contributed 87 off 171 balls.

Bangladesh 'A' finished the day's play on 471 for six, still trailing South Africa Africa 'A' by 41 runs after the hosts posted 512 in their first innings.
